extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of 19th-century literary-philosophical essays (readers of Carlyle's Sartor Resartus)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted normative claims and evaluative principles embedded in Carlyle's Sartor Resartus chapters on Church‑Clothes, Symbols, Helotage, the Phoenix, and Old Clothes. These are prescriptive/descriptive criteria about religion, symbols, social dignity, and manners set out in literary-philosophical prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three states of Church/Society (preaching/struggling/dumb)
rubrics_metrics.description: Societies/Churches may be (1) 'an audibly preaching and prophesying Church' (the best), (2) 'a Church that struggles to preach and prophesy, but cannot as yet, till its Pentecost come', or (3) 'a Church gone dumb with old age, or which only mumbles delirium prior to dissolution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This taxonomy is used to judge the vitality of a society's religious/spiritual life: active preaching/prophesying is healthiest; striving but not yet realized is intermediate; silence and delirious mumbling indicate decay and impending dissolution. ('Whoso fancies that by Church is here meant Chapter-houses and Cathedrals... let him read on.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Church‑Clothes as essential social tissues
rubrics_metrics.description: Without Vestures and sacred Tissues (Church‑Clothes) 'Society has not existed, and will not exist.' Government is the outward skin, Craft‑Guilds are the flesh, and Religion is the inmost pericardial and nervous tissue that ministers life and warm circulation to the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutions and outward forms by whether they serve the animating spiritual function. If religion (the inner tissue) is absent, society becomes only gregarious and will 'gradually issue in universal selfish discord...the very dust and dead body of Society would have evaporated.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity vs sham in religious forms (sham‑priest warning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish true priests/interpreters of the holy from 'Sham-priest (Schein-priester) the falsest and basest'; canonical garments that lack inward spirit are hollow masks under which 'only spiders and unclean beetles' dwell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: venerating outward clerical trappings that lack inner life; prophecy that such canonicals 'will one day be torn from him' and used as bandages or tinder. Judge religious forms by their living spirit, not by external splendor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of Silence and Secrecy for thought and virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The benignant efficacies of Concealment... SILENCE and SECRECY!' — Silence is the element in which great things fashion themselves together; 'Speech is too often... of quite stifling and suspending Thought.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for intellectual and moral work: prefer restraint in speaking while creating; hold tongue to clarify purpose; practice secrecy as soil in which virtue grows ('Like other plants, Virtue will not grow unless its root be hidden'). Anti-pattern: indiscriminate publicizing of projects or prating that suspends thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols combine concealment and revelation to embody the Infinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A Symbol contains 'concealment and yet revelation' so that 'the Infinite is made to blend itself with the Finite... attainable there.' Symbols guide, command, and frame human life by making invisible forces visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate symbolic acts, devices, and works of art by whether they allow Eternity/the Infinite to 'look through' Time — i.e., whether they give palpable access to deeper truths. Strong symbols fuse high speech and noble silence for 'double significance.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish intrinsic vs extrinsic value of symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Many symbols have only extrinsic value (accidental standards that unite multitudes, e.g., clouted shoe, wallets of the Gueux, heraldic coats). Intrinsic symbols are 'of themselves fit that men should unite round it' (true works of art, religious symbols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: prefer and cultivate symbols with intrinsic meaning (that manifest the Godlike) rather than mere external badges whose value derives only from association. Recognize when a symbol's value is accidental/extrinsic and when it embodies genuine, enduring significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works of art and lives of heroes as highest symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: True Works of Art (and noble lives) are those in which 'Eternity looking through Time' appears; the life of heroic god‑inspired men is counted 'nobler than all' as the highest form of symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge art and biography by their capacity to reveal perennial, transcendent meaning; such works accrue intrinsic divineness over time and may acquire added sacredness through human reverence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols age and must be judged/removed with prudence
rubrics_metrics.description: As Time progresses, symbols 'at length defaces, or even desecrates them; and Symbols, like all terrestrial Garments, wax old.' A wise legislator 'can so much as tell when a Symbol has grown old, and gently remove it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for cultural reform: recognize when ceremonial solemnities and pageants have become empty and decide to retire or reinterpret them gently rather than cling blindly. Plant for eternity by addressing deep faculties; plant for day by addressing shallow faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative faculty trumps mechanical calculation of motives
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Not our Logical, Mensurative faculty, but our Imaginative one is King over us... Fantasy is thy eye, with its color-giving retina.' The mechanistic Doctrine of Motives reduces human life wrongly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate social theories and individual conduct in light of imagination and fantasy rather than reducing human action to calculable motives; resist mechanizing moral and political life into mere motive‑grinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor both the toilworn craftsman and the inspired thinker/artist
rubrics_metrics.description: Two men to honor: (1) 'the toilworn Craftsman' who conquers Earth for daily bread, and (2) 'Him who is seen toiling for the spiritually indispensable' (artist/thinker). Highest honor when outward toil and inward striving unite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social valuation criterion: esteem manual laborers for their indispensable bodily work and esteem artists/thought‑workers for spiritual nourishment; prize the synthesis of both (e.g., 'Peasant Saint'). Policies and culture should aim to impart knowledge and spiritual light to all, not merely material sustenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemn treating the poor as disposable (critique of Helotage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Satirical exposure of proposals to repress population ('hunt down their Helots... shoot all the able-bodied Paupers') and of calculating the value of a man purely economically ('A full-formed Man is not only worth nothing... could afford him a round sum would he simply engage to go and hang himself').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral criterion: reject utilitarian schemes that reduce human beings to economic units or disposable masses. Instead, work to prevent the 'lamp of [the poor man's] soul' from going out by imparting knowledge and dignity universally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism of Utilitarian/Mechanizer destruction without re‑creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilitarianism and Mechanizers are 'admirably calculated for destroying, only not for rebuilding!' They spread like a 'Dog-madness' and may tear down institutions without offering true regeneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and reform should avoid pure destructive utilitarianism; reforms must include plans for genuine cultural and spiritual rebuilding (the 'water of Knowledge and of Life') to sustain human development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand cyclical death-rebirth of societies (the Phoenix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Society may undergo a Phoenix-like burning and rebirth: 'That Carcass...is but her mortal coil which she has shuffled off, to assume a nobler.' The timing and cost of such convulsions are uncertain; change is resisted by human nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for historical prudence: acknowledge inevitability of metamorphosis yet be judicious about accelerating or managing it. Accept that some burning may be necessary but be mindful of collateral harm ('When the Phoenix is fanning her funeral pyre, will there not be sparks flying!').

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy/politeness due to all (bounded by discernment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courtesy 'lies in human nature itself, and is due from all men towards all men.' One should reverence the human body as temple and practice broad politeness ('I would bow to every Man with any sort of hat, or with no hat whatever'), but withhold deference when it would pocket vanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social-moral criterion: cultivate universal good-breeding and education ('each man were then also his neighbor's schoolmaster'), treating all persons with respect while retaining moral discernment so that courtesy is not exploited by vanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect outward shells when they truly symbolize human worth
rubrics_metrics.description: There is merit in reverencing 'Empty, or even Cast Clothes' — outer husks that serve as 'the pure emblem and effigies of Man' — when they no longer enshrine devilish passion but represent human dignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for social comportment: allow outward forms and dress to function as civil emblems that foster mutual respect, provided they are not mere masks for vice. Distinguish genuine emblematic function from hollow pageantry.
